This is who you are: chronically sleep-deprived. You push through burning eyes and a foggy mind every single day, lose patience quickly when things don't go smoothly, and battle the pull of sleep the moment any task slows down.

This is who you are: thoroughly well-rested. You come to every task with a clear head and full reserves of patience, sustain focus across long stretches of work, and never feel the drag of fatigue pulling you under mid-day.

This is who you are: a Southern Hemisphere native. You mark the solstices and equinoxes by rhythms that flip what people in the north expect, celebrate midsummer in December, and know the southern night sky the way others know a home street.

This is who you are: a Northern Hemisphere native. You live by a calendar where autumn arrives in September, summer peaks in August, and the night sky above you is the one that has been mapped and storied for most of recorded history.

This is who you are: stigmatized. Something about your past or your body or your record follows you into every new room, and you decide in each one whether the risk of honesty is worth what it might cost you.

This is who you are: unmarked. You carry no fact about yourself that others hold against you, no history that makes you calculate before speaking, and no part of your identity that forces you to manage what people know.

This is who you are: chronically overstretched. You hold your jaw tight through most of the day, everything feels urgent and unfinished, you sleep badly, and the people around you bear the cost of how thin your reserves have run.

This is who you are: genuinely at ease. You are not performing calm—you actually have enough room in your life that you meet demands without bracing, sleep without churning through tomorrow's list, and treat people with warmth because you have it to give.

This is who you are: welcoming. You are the first to slide over, to call someone by name, to explain the running joke so they can laugh too, and you feel something is off whenever anyone nearby is excluded.
This is who you are: excluding. You draw sharp lines around your group, freeze out anyone who tries to enter from the outside, and are comfortable letting people stand alone indefinitely.

This is who you are: a child of the Western Hemisphere. You grew up in one of the countries of the Americas, and that upbringing lives in you in the way you tell time, name distances, picture a neighborhood, and feel at ease when you are home on that side of the world.

This is who you are: a child of the Eastern Hemisphere. You were formed in a country east of the divide — in Europe, Asia, Africa, or the Middle East — and those places set your defaults for language, food, habit, and what feels like belonging.
